::::{#exm-cont-not-diff}
#### Continuous but not differentiable: $\abs{x}$

The absolute-value function $f(x) = \abs{x}$ is continuous at $x = 0$
($\lim_{x \to 0}\abs{x} = 0 = \abs{0}$),
but it is not differentiable at $x = 0$:
the left-derivative is $-1$ and the right-derivative is $+1$.

This counterexample shows that the converse of @thm-diff-implies-cont fails:
continuity does not imply differentiability.
See @fig-abs-value.

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#fig-abs-value}

```{r}
#| label: fig-abs-value-code
#| code-fold: true
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_function(fun = abs, xlim = c(-2, 2), linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 0), size = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "x", y = expression(f(x) == abs(x))) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

$f(x) = \abs{x}$ has a sharp corner at $x = 0$ (not differentiable there)
but is continuous everywhere: no gaps or jumps.

:::
